title: Fines for Land Encroachment and Occupation: Decree 123/2024
desc: Fines for land encroachment under Decree 123/2024/ND-CP: VND 3 million to 500 million by land type, area, commune or ward; restoration orders.
summary: Fines for encroaching on or occupying land under Article 13 of Decree 123/2024/ND-CP, orders to restore the land, return of illegal gains and whether a red book can be issued for the encroached land.
body: p

Building a fence that encroaches on a neighbour's land, extending onto the pavement or a drainage ditch, or occupying public land is a common violation when building a house. The fines are set out in Article 13 of Decree 123/2024/ND-CP on administrative penalties in the land sector.
h2
1. Fines for encroachment and occupation in communes
p

The fine depends on the land type and the area encroached or occupied. For non-agricultural land (residential land, construction land, etc.) not managed by State agencies, within the boundaries of a commune (Clause 4, Article 13):
ul
Under 0.02 ha (under 200 m²): VND 5–10 million.
From 0.02 to under 0.05 ha: VND 10–30 million.
From 0.05 to under 0.1 ha: VND 30–50 million.
From 0.1 to under 0.5 ha: VND 50–100 million.
From 0.5 to under 1 ha: VND 100–150 million; 1 ha or more: VND 150–200 million.
p

For agricultural land (other than rice land and forest land) in a commune, fines start at VND 3–5 million for an area under 0.02 ha; encroaching on or occupying rice land or forest land starts at VND 5–10 million (Clauses 2 and 3, Article 13). Encroaching on or occupying land managed by State agencies or organisations in a commune starts at VND 3–5 million, up to VND 150–200 million (Clause 1, Article 13).
h2
2. Fines in wards are doubled
p

Encroaching on or occupying land within the boundaries of a ward or town is fined 2 times the corresponding level in communes, up to VND 500 million for individuals and VND 1 billion for organisations (Clause 6, Article 13). The fines in the Decree apply to individuals; organisations are fined 2 times as much (Clause 2, Article 5).
p

Encroaching on or occupying the safety protection corridor of works (roads, dykes, power grids, etc.) is fined under the specialised law; if the specialised law has no provision, this Decree applies (Clause 7, Article 13).
h2
3. What else is ordered besides the fine?
ul
Restoring the original condition of the land, including the plot boundaries and markers – that is, demolishing fences and works on the encroached land (Clause 8, Article 13).

Returning illegal gains: calculated on the value of the land use right of the encroached or occupied area under the land price table, the area and the number of years of violation (Point b, Clause 2, Article 6).
The violating area is measured against the cadastral map; if the violator disagrees with the result, they may hire a surveying unit to re-measure at their own cost (Article 7).
h2
4. Can encroached land get a red book?
p

Restoration is not ordered if that land meets the conditions for a Certificate or may be used temporarily under Article 139 of the Land Law. Article 139 applies only to violations before 1 July 2014; land encroaching on the protection corridor of public works, roadbed, road shoulder or pavement after the boundary line has been announced is reclaimed and no Certificate is issued (Clause 1, Article 139).
h2
5. Advice when building a house
ol
Before building, have a surveyor mark the boundaries according to the red book and draw up a record with the neighbours.
Do not build fences, entrance steps or canopies that extend onto the road, pavement or drainage ditch.
Build in line with the permit – see Fines for Building Without a Permit or Contrary to a Permit (fines under construction law are separate).
If there is a boundary dispute, seek mediation at the ward or commune People's Committee before continuing.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The limitation period for fining land violations is 2 years (Article 3). Decree 123/2024/ND-CP is shown as partially no longer in effect on the National Legal Portal; the articles cited have not been found amended in our library. With the abolition of the district level, the authority to impose fines and the names of administrative units (ward, town) may have been adjusted by documents on two-level local government that are not in our library – ask the ward or commune People's Committee where the land is located.
